clue.text: Musician did not start aid

indicators.note: the musician's word loses its opening letter, since it did not start as it normally would

parts.note: a bassist is a musician who plays bass guitar or double bass

explanation.surface: A musician failed to get some help off the ground.
explanation.definitionFit: To help someone is to give them support, so aid and this verb or noun are synonyms.

clue.text: Opera gig reproducing chord

indicators.note: reproducing here means making again in a new form, so the letters of the two words are rearranged

explanation.surface: A singer's performance at the opera recreates a particular chord.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reproducing' signals the anagram of OPERA GIG.
explanation.definitionFit: A broken chord whose notes are played one after another rather than together.

clue.text: Profligate person holding American strap

indicators.note: holding means the first word for a wasteful person grips the next piece inside it

parts.note: a profligate is a wastrel, someone who spends freely

explanation.surface: A spendthrift is clutching a strap from America.
explanation.walkthrough: 'holding' is the container signal; 'strap' is the definition, a stocking holder rather than a man who spends.
explanation.definitionFit: A garter-like band holding up a stocking is a kind of elastic strap.

clue.text: Almost certain way through mountains will go beyond

indicators.note: almost means not quite all of the word, so its final letter is dropped

parts.note: certain means sure
a pass is a route through a mountain range

explanation.surface: A traveller confident of a mountain route plans to press on beyond it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Almost' cuts the last letter from SURE, leaving SUR.
explanation.definitionFit: To exceed or outdo something is to go further than it.

clue.text: Stuck in the water? Hardly!

parts.note: a ship stuck fast in frozen sea is not really in water at all, since the water has turned solid around it

explanation.definitionFit: A vessel trapped by frozen sea is held fast, with the liquid around it turned solid.

clue.text: Rely on advertisement for financial institution

indicators.note: in a down clue, one piece sitting on another comes below it, so the word for rely goes second

parts.note: a commercial is a television or radio advertisement
to bank on something is to rely on it

explanation.surface: Someone advises depending on advertising to promote a bank.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rely on' reads as a phrasal verb, but 'on' is the down-clue placement signal, putting the word for rely beneath the advertisement.
explanation.definitionFit: A high-street lender taking deposits and making loans is one type of money-handling organisation.

clue.text: Benjamin about to go without stain

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the short name goes round the other piece

parts.note: Ben is a short form of Benjamin
to lack is to go without something

explanation.surface: A man called Benjamin is going out without a stain on his character.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' is the container signal; 'to go without' is one piece, a verb meaning do without.
explanation.definitionFit: To blacken something is to dirty or discolour it, so it works as a synonym for marking with a stain.

clue.text: Single person takes article to the angolan rebels

parts.note: a unit is a single individual thing or person
a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: One person brings a piece of writing to rebel fighters in Angola.
explanation.definitionFit: The National Union for the Total Independence of Angola was the insurgent movement in Angola's civil war, known by these initials.

clue.text: Mishandled ragged sword

indicators.note: mishandled means handled badly or jumbled, so the letters of the next word are rearranged

explanation.surface: A tattered sword has been badly treated.
explanation.definitionFit: A short stabbing blade is a small kind of sword.

clue.text: Police officer meaning to be controlling

parts.note: super is short for superintendent, a senior police officer
meaning to do something is intending to do it

explanation.surface: A police officer has every intention of taking charge.
explanation.definitionFit: Overseeing or directing work is the same as being in control of it.

clue.text: Sitter that's also a baffling problem

explanation.surface: An artist's model who also turns out to be a puzzle.
explanation.definitionFit: A sitter for a portrait strikes a pose; a hard question that puzzles someone is also called by this word.

clue.text: Signifying nothing in one French sense

parts.note: un is French for one
the sense of a word is its meaning

explanation.surface: A French phrase that says nothing at all.
explanation.definitionFit: Something without significance carries no content or purport.

clue.text: Grandee defused bomb

indicators.note: defused suggests something taken apart, so the letters of the nobleman's title are rearranged

explanation.surface: A nobleman made a bomb safe.
explanation.definitionFit: A hand-thrown explosive is a small bomb.

clue.text: Sleek ad about valley in lake district

indicators.note: about can mean round and around, so the letters of the two words are turned into a new order

explanation.surface: A glossy advertisement for a Cumbrian valley.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' here is the anagram signal on SLEEK AD. The Lake District is a mountainous national park in north-west England.
explanation.definitionFit: A valley of the River Esk in Cumbria, in north-west England's lakeland.

clue.text: Fuzziness inside separate headland

parts.note: in means inside
distinct means separate or different
a ness is a promontory, as in place names like Loch Ness's neighbour Orford Ness

explanation.surface: Blurriness inside a detached headland.
explanation.definitionFit: Lack of sharpness or clarity is blurriness, the quality of not being clear.

clue.text: The lady repeatedly left with cod perhaps or oysters

parts.note: she refers to a lady

indicators.note: repeatedly means the single letter for left appears twice

parts.note: cod is an example of a fish

explanation.surface: A woman keeps leaving with cod or oysters for supper.
explanation.definitionFit: Oysters are molluscs with hard cases, a type of edible sea creature.

clue.text: Like the finest old style fireproof material

parts.note: as means like
best means the finest
OS is the abbreviation for Old Style, the calendar dating before 1752

explanation.surface: A fireproof material of old, said to be the very finest.
explanation.definitionFit: A fibrous mineral once widely used for insulation because it does not burn.

clue.text: Tommy's home?

parts.note: a Tommy is a British army private soldier, so his home would be a private soldier's lodging, read differently as a confidential place of residence

explanation.walkthrough: Tommy, or Tommy Atkins, is a traditional name for an ordinary British soldier.
explanation.definitionFit: A home location kept confidential, cheekily pictured as where an army private lives.

clue.text: Five books include operatic song in slightly different form

indicators.note: include means the first pieces hold the song within them

parts.note: V is the Roman numeral for five
NT is the New Testament, books of the Bible
an aria is a solo song in an opera

explanation.surface: Five volumes contain an aria in an altered version.
explanation.walkthrough: 'include' is the container signal, with the numeral and the scripture abbreviation together forming the outside.
explanation.definitionFit: An alternative version that differs slightly from the standard one.

clue.text: Old Greek settler

parts.note: not a colonist from ancient Greece but the coin that once settled bills in Greece before the euro

explanation.definitionFit: The former currency unit of Greece, used to settle debts before the euro.

clue.text: Monkey, he is in western half of Russia

indicators.note: in means the contracted pronoun phrase goes inside the half-country
the western half of a word written left to right is its first half

parts.note: he's is the contraction of he is

explanation.surface: A monkey, he is found in the west of Russia.
explanation.walkthrough: 'western half of' takes the first three of the country's six letters; 'in' is the container signal. 'Monkey, he is' reads as a description but splits into definition and fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: The rhesus macaque is a brown South Asian monkey.

clue.text: Safe place on course when baseball player gets round

parts.note: home is a safe place
a run is a course, as in a ski run

explanation.surface: A secure spot on a track as a batter circles the bases.
explanation.definitionFit: In baseball, a hit letting the batter circle all bases and score in one go.

clue.text: Grinding backbiter

parts.note: not a spiteful gossip but a back tooth that grinds food

explanation.definitionFit: A broad back tooth used for chewing and grinding.

clue.text: Outstanding type

parts.note: not an excellent person but print whose characters stand out, raised from the page for reading by touch

explanation.definitionFit: A system of raised dots read by touch by blind people.

clue.text: Army to the rescue?

parts.note: the word means rescue or deliverance and also names the Christian charity army

explanation.definitionFit: Deliverance from harm or sin, and the first word of the charity's name.

clue.text: It elevates one amongst the crowd

indicators.note: amongst means placed among, so the numeral goes inside the word for a crowd

parts.note: a host is a large crowd
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A device that lifts one person above the crowd.
explanation.definitionFit: A lifting device such as a crane raises loads, so it is something that lifts things up.

clue.text: Arty gets revised plan

indicators.note: revised means altered or reworked, so the letters of the two words are rearranged

explanation.surface: An arty person gets a revised scheme.
explanation.walkthrough: 'revised' signals the anagram of ARTY GETS.
explanation.definitionFit: An overall scheme for achieving a goal is a plan.

clue.text: Bachelor Thomas found it was an anticlimax

parts.note: a, the indefinite article, stands in for an
Thos is the traditional written abbreviation of Thomas

explanation.surface: A single man named Thomas found an event a letdown.
explanation.walkthrough: 'found it was' links the pieces to the definition; the A comes from 'an', placed between B and THOS.
explanation.definitionFit: A sudden drop from the sublime to the trivial produces a ludicrous letdown.
